reasons: Lake identity gives case_name_full as Arkansas v. Sanders, court as U.S., court_level as scotus, year as 1979, and date_decided as 1979-06-20.
Lake citations list official cite 442 U.S. 753, parallel cites 99 S. Ct. 2586 and 61 L. Ed. 2d 235, and vendor-neutral cite 1979 U.S. LEXIS 6.

defect.evidence_quote: In earlier cases, on the other hand, the Court sustained the constitutionality of warrantless searches of automobiles and their contents under what has become known as the “automobile exception” to the warrant requirement.
defect.problem: The case is properly connected to the Automobile Exception, but the role label 'Historical / origin' is overbroad unless 'origin' is understood as the origin of the former luggage/container limitation, not the origin of the automobile exception itself.
defect.proposed_fix: Change the home role to something like 'Historical / former container limitation' or 'Historical / luggage-container rule' rather than unqualified 'Historical / origin'.

reasons: The opinion expressly frames the case as deciding whether Sanders falls on the Chadwick or Chambers/Carroll side of the automobile-exception line.
The opinion also says prior cases had already established what became known as the automobile exception, so Sanders did not originate that exception as a whole.
residual_risks: The 'Historical' component depends on treatment/currency, which lens A does not decide.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Qualify the role so it points to the former personal-luggage/container rule within the automobile-exception doctrine.

defect.evidence_quote: Thus, insofar as the police are entitled to search such luggage without a warrant, their actions must be justified under some exception to the warrant requirement other than that applicable to automobiles stopped on the highway.
defect.problem: The main holding is supported, but 'absent exigency' is slightly too narrow because the Court said a warrantless search would need some warrant exception other than the automobile exception, not only exigency.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace 'absent exigency' with 'unless another warrant exception, independent of the automobile exception, applies.'

reasons: The p. 766 holding supports that the Fourth Amendment warrant requirement applies to personal luggage taken from an automobile to the same degree as luggage elsewhere.
The opinion supports that once police have seized and secured the suitcase, automobile mobility does not itself justify a warrantless search.
The opinion preserves other warrant exceptions; it is more precise to say the automobile exception alone does not justify the search.
residual_risks: The 'later overruled by California v. Acevedo' clause is treatment/currency and is reserved for lens B.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use the Court's own formulation: personal luggage taken from an automobile generally requires a warrant unless the search is justified by an exception other than the automobile exception.

Under lens A, no finding is made on whether the treatment/current-law status is substantively correct.
residual_risks: Treatment/currency was not assessed under this lens.

residual_risks: Treatment/currency effects on practical authority weight are reserved for lens B.
